history.dynasty: Mewar (one travel site attributes the build to the reign of Maharana Raj Singh - verify)
history.summary: The famous old-city Ganesh temple of Udaipur, on Bohra Ganesh Road near Mohanlal Sukhadia University and the Govt. Ahad Museum (Dhoolkot area). Believed about 350 years old; originally named 'Borganesh' and built outside the then city boundary, with the surrounding locality now also called Bohra Ganesh. The name's story: about 70-80 years ago, people who needed money for marriage or business would write the amount on a slip of paper and leave it before the idol; the amount would arrive and had to be returned with interest - and since money-lending is associated with the Bohra community, the Ganesh here came to be called Bohra Ganesh. The east-facing idol is in a dancing/standing posture and is considered highly efficacious (Chamatkarik), earning the temple the same respect in Udaipur as Moti Dungari enjoys in Jaipur; Wednesday is the special weekly day. Coordinates are Wikipedia's published values (24.58957083, 73.727688833).

name: Bohra Ganesh Temple
town_description: Udaipur, the 'City of Lakes' in southern Rajasthan, was founded as the capital of the Mewar kingdom by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1559. Set among the Aravalli hills around Lake Pichola and Fateh Sagar, it is one of India's most visited heritage cities, known for its palaces, temples and old-city lanes.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport (Udaipur), about 23 km east.
travel.railway: Udaipur City railway station, about 4 km away.
travel.road: Bohra Ganesh Road, near Mohanlal Sukhadia University and the Ahad Museum, about 2 km from the city centre; reached by taxi or auto-rickshaw.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Wednesdays and Ganesh Chaturthi draw the biggest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: One source lists 6:00 AM-8:00 PM daily - not consistently published, verify on arrival.
